## 固定收益市場主線

科技股再度重挫，促使投資人轉向公債避險，美國公債買盤也擴及長天期。10年期殖利率下跌7.56個基點至4.8541%，30年期下跌7.24個基點至5.2479%。當日債市漲勢由實質殖利率下降帶動，油價回升則伴隨通膨補償小幅上揚；同時，美國通膨與成長數據仍支撐聯準會12月升息的預期。

午後股市回升，縮小了當日跌幅，公債的避險需求仍在。那斯達克100指數盤中一度下跌4.7%，收盤跌幅收斂至0.64%。企業債的壓力則更集中於個別信用風險：標普將Nvidia評等列入可能降評的觀察名單，CoreWeave信用違約保護成本再創新高；銀行正為CoreWeave籌備有擔保貸款，討論中的定價與其無擔保債殖利率形成鮮明落差。

10月實質消費支出持平，為美債漲勢提供了需求轉弱的依據，但核心PCE年增率加快至3.3%，第三季經濟成長率也上修至4.3%。投資人一面為金融市場動盪尋求即時保護，一面仍須面對各國央行因物價壓力持續而維持的政策約束。

## 美債買盤擴大，美國需求訊號分歧

上午股市急跌期間，美債漲勢加速，那斯達克100指數一度較收盤高點下跌20%。據Bloomberg報導，2至10年期美債殖利率盤中跌幅均曾達至少10個基點，10年期降至9月9日以來最低。Fort Washington Investment Advisors的Dan Carter認為，股市走弱促使投資人轉向信用品質較高的資產。

隨後股票買盤回流。標普500指數盤中最多下跌3.2%，最終收在7,182.78點，僅跌0.25%；那斯達克100指數收在26,046.90點。道瓊指數上漲約0.3%，標普500多數成分股也上漲。市場廣度顯示，賣壓並未遍及所有類股：科技股持續承壓，其他類股則吸引資金。Nvidia下跌3.9%。VIX在拋售期間一度逼近35，收盤報28.29，上漲7.32%。

美債買盤延續前一日由中天期主導的反彈，進一步擴至長天期。2年期殖利率下跌4.14個基點至4.6415%，5年期下跌6.38個基點至4.6693%。10年期跌幅較大，使2年與10年期利差收窄3.42個基點至21.26個基點；30年期加入漲勢後，2年與30年期利差也收窄3.1個基點至60.64個基點。

與一週前相比，5年與10年期仍是反彈最強的券種，殖利率分別下跌21.84與21.42個基點，2年與30年期則分別下跌16.27與16.2個基點。週三長債買盤擴大了中天期已相當明顯的反彈。Bloomberg市場報導指出，10年期殖利率已連續八天下跌，是2024年以來最長紀錄。

當日殖利率下降的構成有明顯變化。10年期實質殖利率下跌7.93個基點至2.7207%，損益兩平通膨率則上升0.37個基點至2.1334%。一週以來，實質殖利率下降15個基點，通膨補償下降6.42個基點；拉長至一個月，實質殖利率仍上升7.92個基點，損益兩平通膨率則下跌21.96個基點。此前名目債券反彈較多來自通膨補償下降，本日實質借款成本則明顯回落。

債市上漲之際，油價也回升。WTI期貨上漲2.56%至每桶$84.15，布蘭特上漲3.60%至$94.69，但兩者仍分別較一個月前下跌16.63%與15.23%。黃金期貨回升0.74%至每盎司$3,588.40，美元指數下跌0.11%至103.691。黃金稍早表現疲弱，倫敦交易時段現貨金一度跌破$3,500，美元走強、跨市場平倉賣壓及貨幣緊縮預期均壓抑需求。

銅價下跌另反映工業需求信心轉弱。倫敦金屬交易所期銅收跌1.5%，至每公噸$11,649.50，較9月高點下跌逾20%。混沌天成期貨的Li Xuezhi將賣壓歸因於市場擔心AI資本支出下修，以及中國需求疲弱。部分金屬市場的即期供給仍吃緊；不過，LME收緊大額持有者的出借規定後，鋁現貨對3個月期貨的逆價差由週一每噸逾$400縮至$112.58，即期逼倉壓力隨價格下跌而有所緩解。

美國上午公布的數據呈現第三季成長強勁、第四季初放緩的組合。第三季GDP第二次估值的季增年率為4.3%，高於初值3.4%、市場預期3.5%，也快於第二季的2.2%。消費成長由3.8%上修至4.2%，民間投資由19.4%上修至22.4%。其中設備投資成長21.8%、智慧財產產品13.6%、建築物投資9.5%，企業投資與家庭消費同為經濟擴張的主要動力。

存貨對GDP成長貢獻1.64個百分點，出口下滑5.4%、進口增加19.2%，住宅投資則萎縮3.4%。最終銷售成長2.6%，高於前次估計的2.2%。這些構成顯示，生產與投資雖強，存貨累積也是成長加速的重要來源，住宅建築仍然疲弱。企業獲利季增3.8%，低於前季的8.2%，但年增21.3%，為2021年以來最快。

10月家庭支出隨後放緩。名目支出月增0.3%，低於市場預期0.4%，也低於9月上修後的0.6%。實質支出持平，前月修正後為增加0.1%。名目支出增加$638億，其中服務增加$521億、商品增加$118億，汽車與零件支出則減少$139億。家庭也減少家具、餐廳用餐及旅館住宿支出。

所得表現較穩健。個人所得增加0.7%，高於預期0.4%及前月0.3%；可支配所得增加0.8%，實質可支配所得增幅為1月以來最大，儲蓄率升至三個月高點。美國經濟分析局指出，所得增長部分來自Medicare Improvement Fund一次性保費退款，薪資所得也持續增加。Fifth Third Commercial Bank的Bill Adams認為，儘管10月支出暫歇，整體消費趨勢仍穩健；RSM的Joe Brusuelas則強調，總需求強勁加上通膨加速，需要政策回應。

物價細項也顯示，單月消費放緩並未消除通膨壓力。10月核心PCE月增0.3%，與前月及市場預期一致；年增率卻由3.1%升至3.3%，超過預期3.2%，為2023年以來最快。整體PCE月增率由0.5%降至0.3%，年增率由3.7%升至3.8%，兩者均符合預期。排除能源與住宅的服務價格月增0.3%。商品與服務價格仍有上漲壓力，與當月消費停滯同時出現。

其他數據顯示，就業與投資意願仍強。首次申領失業救濟人數由20.2萬降至18.9萬，低於市場預期20萬；續領人數由179.2萬降至169.7萬，也低於預期172.1萬。10月不含飛機的非國防資本財訂單增加1.2%，高於預期0.7%及前月0.5%。耐久財訂單總額僅增0.2%，低於預期0.6%及9月1.8%；不含運輸設備的訂單則增加0.5%，符合預期，並與前月相同。相較於整體訂單，資本財細項釋出的投資訊號更強。

聯準會褐皮書顯示，成本壓力來源廣泛。12個地區中，八個回報成長、四個持平，整體活動略微至溫和擴張，就業略增。薪資與福利由前次報告的小幅上升加快至溫和上升，壓力集中於難以補人的職位，也受到生活成本調整及福利費用影響。受訪者列舉能源、運輸、醫療保健、保險、關稅、原物料與貨運等成本壓力；競爭環境及家庭對價格的敏感度，限制部分企業轉嫁成本的能力。本次調查由亞特蘭大聯準銀行彙編，資料蒐集截至11月16日。

住宅市場對高借款成本的反應同樣不一。10月新屋銷售在前月下跌9.7%後增加14.2%，建築許可終值則繼前月下跌0.4%後再降7.2%。MBA房貸申請增加6.1%，扭轉前次下跌2.3%的走勢；購屋申請指數由137.6升至151.6，轉貸申請僅略有改善。MBA的30年期房貸利率由7.35%微升至7.38%。

Bloomberg另就住宅建商的報導指出，促銷優惠在支撐銷售的同時也侵蝕獲利。標普綜合1500住宅建商指數截至週二年初以來下跌0.9%，較2月高點低16%，可能連續第三年下跌。Meritage、Lennar與NVR的2027年預估毛利率均處於多年低點。Evercore ISI的Stephen Kim指出，勞工短缺與施工週期拉長也推升成本；Bloomberg Intelligence的Drew Reading則認為，若利率持續下降是由通膨降溫帶動，對需求的提振會強於伴隨經濟惡化的降息環境。

美國財政部7年期公債標售得標殖利率為4.71%，低於前次4.89%；投標倍數由2.46略降至2.43。本週供給進入市場時，公債整體行情已明顯走強，帶動標售殖利率下降，但投標倍數小幅回落，顯示需求較前次並非全面改善。

## AI借款人的信用分化加深

科技股拋售使CoreWeave信用違約保護成本再度大幅上升。依ICE Data Services資料，5年期CDS一度上升2.09個百分點，創單日最大升幅，年費率達15.34%。Bloomberg報導，交換合約隱含其未來五年違約機率超過70%。投資人質疑AI產業靠舉債擴張能否取得足夠回報，Nvidia、Alphabet、Oracle與SpaceX的信用保護成本也創新高。

CoreWeave現券同樣承壓。TRACE資料顯示，其2031年到期、票息9%的債券價格跌至新低，殖利率約18%。另一方面，摩根士丹利與三菱日聯金融集團正為其籌備$45億貸款，最快下週銷售，初步討論殖利率約7%至7.5%。知情人士表示，潛在投資人表達的認購意向規模已與擬議交易相當，但細節與時程仍可能調整。

這筆擬議貸款的償付結構與CoreWeave無擔保公司債不同。資金將存入託管帳戶，再按需提領，用於採購喬治亞州Dalton資料中心所需的GPU，相關設備將供Meta Platforms使用。貸款預期在存續期間逐步攤還；雖然CoreWeave本身評等低於投資級，但因有Meta合約支持，這筆債務預期可取得投資級評等。其延後動用定期貸款目前約以面額交易。明確客戶、擔保品與分階段撥款，使討論中的融資成本與公司無擔保債出現顯著差距。

建設規模仍然龐大。Core Scientific正在美國五州開發設施，已依12年期合約全數出租給CoreWeave，可能帶來約$100億營收。CoreWeave第三季資本支出達$145億，前九個月合計$306.5億。新貸款將為擴建的另一部分提供資金，而承擔整體企業風險的公司債持有人要求更高補償。

Nvidia則面臨獨立的評等風險。標普因Jensen Huang離職又復職所暴露的管理與治理弱點，將其AA評等列入負向信用觀察，展開90天審查。除非未來業務前景已受損，標普預期即使降評也僅會下調一級。審查另涵蓋可能違反出口管制的問題，以及董事會架構與組成的有效性。

Huang週一回歸，最初緩解了市場對這家AI生態系核心企業領導層的疑慮；標普的行動則把焦點轉向人事逆轉所衍生的治理問題。Nvidia在美國高評級公司債指數內約有$325億債券，其重要性也延伸至為其他AI企業提供融資及設備。5年期CDS一度上升6個基點，盤中年費率達147.27個基點的新高。穆迪先前已將其Aa1評等展望由正向調為穩定，週三以治理與監管不確定性持續為由，維持展望不變。

跌勢也開始引發對估值的不同看法。DoubleLine的Robert Cohen在11月20日接受、週三刊出的訪問中表示，隨殖利率與利差改善，公司已開始買入AI相關債券。他指出，評等AA的Amazon、Alphabet及Microsoft債券，其利差已接近一般BBB債券水準；投資級SpaceX證券的殖利率接近高收益債，也具有投資價值。他並在研究Oracle，其利差高於同評級企業。

不過，Cohen對投機級新型雲端業者的無擔保債立場更為審慎。他質疑CoreWeave資本結構是否可持續、業務計畫是否已有充分資金，並將融資風險與早年的頁岩產業擴張相比。他在同一投資週期內，區分不同借款人及不同債權的風險。Allspring的Mark Clegg同樣認為，AI債券下跌後更具價值，但價格仍在尋找均衡。美債殖利率下降則支撐債券基金報酬，計入配息後，LQD上漲0.48%，HYG上漲0.12%。

摩根大通的新研究估計，AI產業未來融資需求仍十分龐大。Tarek Hamid與Nathaniel Rosenbaum領導的策略團隊預測，2027年AI相關資本支出將接近倍增至$1.4兆，2028年才趨於平穩。團隊預期，明年公開市場投資級舉債將達$4,500億，高於今年AI企業的$3,680億，另有$650億槓桿融資，以及$250億至$350億證券化產品。

更長期估計顯示，2027至2031年將建置151吉瓦資料中心容量，成本$7兆。由於建設需時多年、資金又須提前籌集，2027年多數建設已取得資金，明年舉債將愈來愈多用於2028年的活動。依預估規模，債市融資能力將逼近上限；摩根大通估計，五年內還需要$2.9兆股權性資金，主要來自超大規模雲端業者自身業務產生的現金流。融資組合也將轉向硬體，2031年GPU資金需求可能超過已具備電力設施的機房建物資金需求的4倍。

各機構預測有明顯差異。高盛預期，超大規模雲端業者明年AI資本支出將增加50%至$1.2兆，Entext則預測增速放緩至約25%。摩根大通認為，2027年底或2028年初可能出現某一季，當時對下一季支出的展望將接近持平。這會讓債券供給更可預測，但投資人也須評估多年快速擴張後，成長大幅放緩的影響。

亞洲方面，美國收緊中國取得先進晶片的限制，已改變銀行放貸決策。知情人士表示，銀行正暫停向字節跳動、阿里巴巴及騰訊提供數十億美元貸款。花旗、渣打、星展及其他貸款機構正審查資料中心客戶，要求補充晶片使用者及遵守美國商務部規定的資料。出租運算資源的新型雲端業者，以及投資亞洲營運商的私募投資人，也收到相關詢問。

壓力並延伸至資產出售談判。由BlackRock與IFM支持的財團，正考慮調降對Stack Infrastructure亞太資料中心的股權收購出價，並讓部分後續付款取決於專案交付。談判曾涉及日本、澳洲與馬來西亞資產，企業價值約$200億至$250億；扣除債務及計畫資本支出後，股權價值將遠低於該金額。當地反對聲浪、電力與水資源限制、核准程序，以及中國遠端需求的不確定性，都使開發中專案的估值更加複雜。

BDA Partners的Paul DiGiacomo表示，基礎需求尚未崩解，但部分平台負債沉重、產能交付仍不確定，估值卻比照科技公司。Liquid Compute的Ronit Jain則指出，晶片規定收緊打亂了部分亞洲營運商服務中國用戶的計畫，這些業者正試圖將過剩運算容量出售給美國客戶。這些商業調整呈現在不同環節：貸款機構更仔細審視合規用戶，買方則重新考量尚待交付產能的合理價格。

阿里巴巴也正與銀行初步討論明年可能發行離岸人民幣或美元債，並爭取中國國家發展和改革委員會的發行額度。百達資產管理的Cary Yeung預期，中國超大規模雲端業者債券的整體殖利率具吸引力、供給又相對有限，需求仍有支撐，但能否取得先進晶片是重要疑慮。討論仍屬初步，市場波動也會影響最終發行安排。

## 企業融資進度不一，市場承接條件轉趨分化

信用市場動盪波及由加拿大大型退休金管理機構之一支持的發行人。La Caisse基礎建設融資平台的發行實體CDP Infrastructures，暫停最高C$10億的首次發債。知情人士指出，市況惡化將迫使發行人接受更寬利差，並可能縮小規模。

這筆擬議5年期債券上週開始行銷時，利差約為公債之上70個基點；本週初已至少擴大5個基點。Morningstar DBRS給予發行人的初步評等為AA，發行人可能稍後再重啟交易。Alphabet上週發行C$60億債券，也讓加拿大公司債投資人仍在消化大批新增供給。歐洲方面，Deutsche Pfandbriefbank延後英鎊債發行，成為該地區2026年首筆撤回的高評級債券交易。

樂天的融資受挫則有更明顯的個別因素。公司週二以多項情況為由，撤回原訂約1,500億日圓的次順位債發行，未決定未來發行時間。樂天證券已證實約441萬筆客戶資料外洩，集團拒絕說明取消發債是否受此事件影響。東京週三上午6時30分，樂天5年期CDS利差約擴大29個基點至262個基點左右，為2025年4月以來最大升幅。行動通訊業務仍持續虧損，取消發債又增添融資疑慮。

大型收購融資仍有提案。銀行向CVC提出最高110億歐元的債務融資，供可能收購Verisure使用，包括面向銀行及機構投資人的槓桿貸款與高收益債；私募信貸業者也爭取參與次順位債務。CVC正在研究出價，目前仍持有約44%股權的Hellman & Friedman，若交易成行，可能保留部分投資。Verisure自斯德哥爾摩上市以來股價已下跌約五分之一，消息傳出後上漲。談判仍在進行，尚不確定是否提出收購要約。

越南HDBank則規劃以國際債券與聯貸籌資。董事長Kim Byoungho表示，銀行計畫發行最高$5億全球債券，期限可能為3年，另正洽談$6億聯貸，兩項籌資均以年底前完成為目標，否則延至2027年第一季。若債券發行完成，將成為首家在英國掛牌債務的越南銀行。Kim表示，該行7月取得的$7.21億聯貸曾獲大幅超額認購。

越南信用成長快於存款，是本次籌資的背景。HDBank今年放款成長目標約35%，部分反映其參與一家較小銀行的重整，全體銀行體系目標則約15%。越南央行本月透過一筆$20億、期限6個月的外匯換匯交易，投放近50兆越南盾，也直接向銀行買入美元。惠譽預期，越南主要銀行至明年底將籌集逾$69億，但提醒多數銀行資本仍薄弱，這波資本籌措不太可能使資本狀況顯著改善。Kim強調，放款擴張之際須維護資產品質與資本適足性。

美國地方政府債市場方面，Firecrest Aerospace已取得摩根大通不可撤銷信用狀，支持其透過威斯康辛州Stevens Point發行的$1,000萬浮動利率債券。債券2046年到期，資金用於無人機引擎製造廠，預計12月1日定價。惠譽基於摩根大通的信用支持，給予AA/F1+評等。信用狀可支付本金與利息，但若未展延或更換，將於2027年12月1日到期；母公司Czechoslovak Group則保證Firecrest對銀行的義務。債券期限遠長於銀行信用支持期限，是這筆融資的重要特徵。

## 通膨使全球利率前景更為複雜

澳洲通膨數據挑戰了近期市場轉向提前降息的預期。10月截尾平均通膨年增率加速至3.8%，高於預期3.6%，核心價格月增0.5%；整體通膨達4.9%，也超過預期4.7%。住宅成本年增6.4%、電價25.2%、新建住宅價格5.1%，車用燃油價格則月增6.3%。

數據公布後，澳元上漲0.2%，對政策敏感的3年期公債殖利率上升4個基點至4.52%。與政策會議連動的市場定價顯示，5月降息機率由公布前57%降至30%。澳洲央行11月稍早在意見分歧下將現金利率升至4.85%，其預測顯示，基礎通膨要到2027年底才會降至2%至3%目標區間上緣以下。

成長限制仍不容忽視。10月就業減少43,500人，失業率升至五年高點，住宅與企業景氣也轉弱，多數經濟學家及交易員仍認為升息循環已結束。野村的Andrew Ticehurst預期，即使通膨接近高峰，澳洲央行仍會維持鷹派立場數月。澳洲聯邦銀行的Hamid Yahyaei認為，數據公布後債券賣壓相對有限，顯示投資人仍相信2027年會降息。通膨意外偏高延後了預期中的政策緩解，但勞動市場轉弱的降息理由仍在。

日本公布的兩項不同指標，都指向物價壓力持續。10月企業服務價格年增率由修正後3.8%加快至4.2%，為1990年以來最快；伊朗戰爭干擾運輸，海運費用大增120.4%，創1986年有資料以來最高。另方面，日本央行排除生鮮食品與特殊因素的消費者物價指標，由3.2%加快至3.5%，是2023年9月以來最快。該指標排除汽油與公用事業補貼等暫時性援助，因此高於政府公布、僅排除生鮮食品的CPI年增率2.2%。

企業同時更清楚感受到借款成本負擔。帝國資料銀行調查中，近59%企業表示升息弊大於利，較12月增加14個百分點。約48%曾被主要往來銀行接洽調高貸款利率；在這些企業中，29%已實際面臨升息。9月新貸款平均利率升至2.12%，為1996年以來最高。在日本央行評估是否從1.25%政策利率再向上調整之際，這些回覆反映了企業對緊縮的切身經驗。

日本40年期公債標售需求轉弱，投標倍數由前次3.10降至2.63，低於過去12個月平均2.75；得標殖利率為4.09%，前次為4.125%。法國巴黎資產管理的Ryutaro Kimura認為，全球避險情緒及殖利率曲線趨平交易的平倉，促使投資人偏好較短天期，而非超長債。2027財政年度預算如何為國防支出與消費稅調降籌資仍不明，也持續影響未來發債展望。

日本最大退休基金GPIF可能帶來較長期的需求變化，但市場對其動向的解讀仍有分歧。GPIF在11月13日董事會討論基本投資組合。摩根大通策略師Junya Tanase認為，這項議程可能表示檢討已進入考量配置調整的階段，最快明年上半年就可能修正，但他明確指出這是推測。GPIF表示，投資環境與原先假設並未顯著偏離，必要時才會考慮調整。目前目標仍是日本國內債券、海外債券、日本國內股票及海外股票各占25%。

英國方面，英國央行總裁Andrew Bailey與副總裁Clare Lombardelli的談話，為進一步升息增加了關鍵支持。Bailey在國會作證時表示，若能源價格未下降，再度升息的可能性高於不升息。他認為經濟比預期更有韌性，勞動市場也由持續轉弱轉為趨於持平。Lombardelli則表示，原先預期的薪資與服務通膨降溫可能已停滯，第二輪效應的證據正在增加。

兩人的立場將影響12月貨幣政策委員會的多數組合。市場反映的升息機率接近80%，多數經濟學家卻預期維持利率至2月。若Bailey與Lombardelli支持升息，加上已主張再升息的委員，可能在九人委員會形成多數。Catherine Mann在11月曾主張升息0.5個百分點，仍支持及早、有力地行動，認為經濟韌性顯示政策限制尚不足。

不過，能源衝擊擴散程度仍有爭議。Bailey表示，企業反映成本難以轉嫁，12月決策將取決於傳導情況，以及新一輪通膨和就業數據。Swati Dhingra則表示，她尚未看到第二輪效應，受影響的消費籃子占比約20%，低於2022年類似階段的70%；她將自己支持11月升息的決定形容為額外保險。英國央行預期，明年夏季通膨將接近5%；家庭能源價格上限將使1月帳單增加26%，4月可能進一步上升。

歐洲央行管理委員會委員、奧地利央行總裁Martin Kocher主張，在通膨更加根深蒂固之前採取行動。他認為前景較9月預測略差，由於遠期能源價格上升，12月對2027年通膨的預測可能需要上修。市場已完全反映12月之後還會再升息一次，他認為依目前資訊，這樣的預期合理。

Kocher區分了持續中的供給衝擊與強勁需求帶動的通膨，表示尚未看到後者。隨薪資談判完成，目前個別可見的第二輪效應可能在2027年上半年更明朗；他也提醒，不能把經濟韌性視為永久不變。另在週三的操作機制討論中，歐洲央行官員對是否將銀行最低準備率由1%提高至2%仍有分歧。知情人士表示，決策可能等到2027年，銀行流動性要求因而暫無立即調整的時間壓力。

## 退休金流入與財政限制牽動新興債市

印度股市回升，使退休基金股票配置逼近監管上限，為公債帶來新增需求。UTI Pension Fund將新增投資的一半配置於主權債，去年則完全未配置；SBI Pension Funds預期，股票僅占新增投資約四分之一，低於截至6月的三個月期間約60%。兩家合計占印度$1,930億退休金市場的58%。

2025年3月監管機構將股票配置上限由15%提高至25%後，基金一度偏好股票，如今配置方向逆轉。今年截至10月，新增退休金投資僅23%流向公債，低於截至2025年3月的財政年度55%。Nifty指數自10月低點回升約14%，現在反而縮小進一步買股的空間。今年聯邦與各邦大量發債，已推動10年期公債殖利率上升逾60個基點，退休金流入有望支撐主權融資。

南非央行關注的則是長期儲蓄資金的另一種競爭。該行週三在金融穩定報告中警告，AI企業舉債可能加劇與政府之間的資金競爭，推高主權融資成本。其分析的國內集合投資計畫，截至第三季近13%資產投資於AI相關企業，其中逾三分之二集中於Nvidia、Apple、Microsoft、Amazon及Alphabet。占約翰尼斯堡股市市值約8%的Naspers與Prosus，也提供間接曝險。

報告指出，全球重新定價可能透過投資組合資金外流、匯率貶值及公債殖利率上升，傳導至南非。從本十年末至2032年，每年到期主權債將接近或超過4,000億南非幣，再融資需求使這段時程格外重要。南非央行仍認為金融體系具有韌性；初步壓力測試顯示，即使嚴重衰退，銀行資本仍會高於監管要求，但緩衝將縮小，完整結果預計2027年初公布。

IMF最新評估則聚焦於降低融資壓力所需的財政調整。基金支持審慎支出與穩定債務，但主張加入明確債務目標、支出上限、初級財政收支目標及修正機制，強化政府目前以原則為本的財政錨。IMF估計，若要在2033年將債務降至GDP約70%，未來三年每年須使初級財政收支改善GDP的0.5%；中期還應將相當於GDP 1%的經常支出，轉向更有效率的公共投資。

IMF預測，今年初級財政盈餘為GDP的1.4%，中期為1.8%，足以讓債務穩定在GDP約75%。南非財政部預測較樂觀，今年為1.7%，2029至2030年達2.9%。薪資談判、國營企業負債、地方政府債務及收入轉弱，仍是風險。IMF也支持維持適度限制性的貨幣政策，使通膨回到央行3%目標，若風險成真，可能需要進一步緊縮。

泰國則面臨較迫切的政治與預算限制。預算局估計，即使將增值稅由7%提高至8.5%，下個財政年度扣除日常支出後，可用於發展及投資的空間也僅約6,740億泰銖，可能創歷史新低。但總理Anutin Charnvirakul已排除加稅，財政部長Ekniti Nitithanprapas也承諾，不調高GDP 70%的債務上限；9月底債務已達68.6%。

經常支出預計將由2026財政年度占預算76%，升至2028年度約82%。若要同時履行上述承諾，投資支出容易受到擠壓。泰國債務結構仍有助融資穩定：逾99%以泰銖計價，平均到期年限超過九年。穆迪認為，相較同評級國家，成長與公共財政持續惡化才是更重要的信用風險；標普預期，至2029年每年經濟成長僅約2.3%至2.4%。目前三大評等機構均給予穩定展望。

政府增收措施包括擴大稅基、檢討租稅優惠，以及對低價網購進口品課稅，但執行不易。央行研究顯示，78%企業及65%勞工屬於非正式部門，4,000萬勞動人口中只有約400萬人繳納個人所得稅。一項擬議的出境旅遊稅因批評而撤回，放棄了估計每年120億泰銖收入。下週提出的中期財政計畫，必須在增收選項有限與債務逼近上限之間取得平衡。

## 後續市場焦點

美國週四感恩節休市，週五債市縮短交易，讓市場消化週三密集經濟數據的時間減少。12月緊縮仍是預期核心，但下一步評估必須同時考量3.3%的核心PCE年增率、上修後強勁的第三季成長、10月實質消費持平，以及金融情勢波動的影響。股票初步反彈後，科技融資調整是否繼續壓縮取得資金的空間，仍待觀察。

CoreWeave最快下週銷售的擬議$45億貸款，是直接的融資考驗。在無擔保債殖利率居高之際，最終定價、規模及配售情況，將呈現投資人如何評價與Meta相關的擔保品及償付結構。Nvidia的90天標普審查取決於治理與監管風險，降評若超過一級，前提是未來業務前景受損。亞洲方面，須觀察銀行如何完成晶片合規審查，以及Stack潛在買方如何在修訂出價中分配建設與交付風險。

美國新提出的關稅架構，為需求與物價增添另一項有條件風險。公布的架構將對中國進口品課徵20%關稅，一位美國高階官員表示，若貿易談判失敗，可能提高至40%。歐盟、日本、南韓與瑞士將面臨15%關稅；對印度擬議的17%稅率則取決於貿易協定能否完成。中國外交部呼籲維護貿易休戰。談判與落實情況，將決定下一波貿易衝擊的程度。

英國12月17日、日本12月18日的利率決策，都將面對通膨持續與借款成本上升的最新證據。英國接下來的就業與物價數據，將影響央行內部對能源成本轉嫁的爭論；日本央行則須衡量補貼調整後通膨加速，以及企業反映融資更昂貴的情況。澳洲政策前景同樣取決於10月通膨高於預期後，就業轉弱是否伴隨物價降溫。較近的主權政策焦點是泰國下週中期財政計畫，增值稅假設與維持債務上限的承諾仍待協調。

overall_summary.headline: 科技股下跌引發避險需求，美債漲勢擴及長天期
overall_summary.session_narrative:
科技股再度遭到拋售，美債需求擴至長天期。10年期殖利率下跌7.56個基點至4.8541%，30年期下跌7.24個基點至5.2479%。10年期實質殖利率下跌7.93個基點，是名目公債上漲的主因；油價回升之際，損益兩平通膨率微升0.37個基點。那斯達克100指數盤中最多下跌4.7%，收盤跌幅縮小至0.64%；即使股票收復大部分失地，公債仍獲支撐。

經濟數據同時呈現10月實質消費支出持平、核心PCE年增率加快至3.3%，以及第三季GDP成長率上修至4.3%。單月消費轉弱有利債券需求，但物價壓力持續，仍支撐12月緊縮預期。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasury buying spread to the long end as another violent retreat in technology shares sent investors into government debt, even as U.S. inflation and growth figures sustained expectations of a December Federal Reserve increase. The 10-year yield fell 7.56 basis points to 4.8541%, while the 30-year declined 7.24 basis points to 5.2479%. Lower real yields accounted for the daily advance, with inflation compensation edging higher as oil recovered.

An afternoon equity recovery reduced the scale of the stock-market losses without extinguishing demand for safety. The Nasdaq 100 finished 0.64% lower after falling as much as 4.7% intraday. In corporate debt, the pressure became more specific: S&P placed Nvidia's rating under review for a possible downgrade, CoreWeave's protection costs reached another record, and its bankers prepared a secured loan whose expected pricing differed sharply from the yield on its unsecured bonds.

October's flat real consumer spending gave the Treasury rally a softer demand observation, but core PCE inflation accelerated to 3.3% annually and Q3 growth was revised to 4.3%. The session paired immediate protection against financial-market turbulence with continuing restraint from central banks confronting persistent prices.

## Treasury Buying Broadens Alongside Mixed U.S. Demand

The Treasury advance intensified during the morning equity rout, when the Nasdaq 100 briefly fell 20% below its closing peak. Bloomberg reported declines of at least 10 basis points at one stage in yields from two through 10 years, with the 10-year reaching its lowest level since September 9. Fort Washington Investment Advisors' Dan Carter attributed the move to investors seeking higher-quality assets as stocks weakened.

Buyers subsequently returned to equities. The S&P 500 recovered most of an intraday decline of as much as 3.2% to finish at 7,182.78, down 0.25%, while the Nasdaq 100 closed at 26,046.90. The Dow gained about 0.3%, and most S&P constituents advanced. That breadth distinguished the session from a uniform liquidation: technology remained under pressure while other sectors attracted money. Nvidia lost 3.9%. The VIX ended at 28.29, up 7.32%, after approaching 35 during the selloff.

Treasury gains nevertheless extended beyond the intermediate maturities that had led the previous day's recovery. The two-year yield fell 4.14 basis points to 4.6415%, and the five-year declined 6.38 basis points to 4.6693%. The larger 10-year decline narrowed the two- to 10-year spread by 3.42 basis points to 21.26 basis points. The two- to 30-year gap contracted 3.1 basis points to 60.64 as the long bond joined the rally.

The weekly comparison still showed the strongest recovery in five- and 10-year debt, with yields down 21.84 and 21.42 basis points respectively. Two-year yields were 16.27 basis points lower and 30-year yields down 16.2. Wednesday's long-end buying thus broadened a recovery already well established in intermediate maturities. Bloomberg's market account described an eighth consecutive daily decline in 10-year yields, the longest sequence since 2024.

The composition of the daily move changed materially. The 10-year real yield declined 7.93 basis points to 2.7207%, while the breakeven inflation rate increased 0.37 basis point to 2.1334%. Over the week, the real yield was down 15 basis points and inflation compensation 6.42. Over the month, however, the real yield remained 7.92 basis points higher, alongside a 21.96-basis-point decline in the breakeven. The latest session brought substantial relief in real borrowing costs after a period in which lower inflation compensation had carried more of the nominal bond recovery.

Oil moved higher during that rally. WTI futures gained 2.56% to $84.15 a barrel and Brent rose 3.60% to $94.69, although both remained sharply below their month-earlier levels, by 16.63% and 15.23%. Gold futures recovered 0.74% to $3,588.40 an ounce, and the dollar index eased 0.11% to 103.691. Those closing moves followed a much weaker earlier period for bullion: spot gold had fallen below $3,500 during London trading as a stronger dollar, liquidation across markets and expectations of monetary tightening weighed on demand.

Copper's decline supplied a separate signal of deteriorating industrial sentiment. London Metal Exchange futures settled 1.5% lower at $11,649.50 a metric ton, more than 20% below their September peak. Chaos Ternary Futures' Li Xuezhi linked the selling to concern about downward revisions to AI capital expenditure and weak Chinese demand. Prompt supply remained tight in parts of the metals market. Aluminum's cash-to-three-month backwardation nevertheless narrowed to $112.58 a ton from more than $400 on Monday after the LME tightened lending rules for large holders, easing an immediate squeeze as outright prices fell.

The U.S. morning releases showed a strong third quarter followed by a slower start to the fourth. GDP expanded at a 4.3% annualized rate in the second estimate, up from the initial 3.4%, above the 3.5% consensus and faster than Q2's 2.2%. Consumption growth was revised to 4.2% from 3.8%, and private investment to 22.4% from 19.4%. Equipment rose 21.8%, intellectual-property products 13.6% and structures 9.5%, placing business investment alongside households as a major source of expansion.

The composition also included a 1.64-percentage-point contribution from inventories. Exports fell 5.4%, imports rose 19.2% and residential investment contracted 3.4%. Final sales grew 2.6%, compared with 2.2% previously. Those details qualify the headline acceleration: production and investment were strong, but inventory accumulation contributed significantly and residential building remained weak. Corporate profits increased 3.8% from the preceding quarter, compared with an 8.2% prior increase, while their 21.3% annual gain was the fastest since 2021.

October household spending then slowed. Nominal outlays rose 0.3%, below the 0.4% consensus and September's upwardly revised 0.6% increase. Real spending was flat after a revised 0.1% gain. The $63.8 billion increase in nominal expenditure included $52.1 billion in services and $11.8 billion in goods, with motor vehicles and parts down $13.9 billion. Households also reduced purchases of furnishings, restaurant meals and hotel stays.

Income provided a firmer offset. Personal income rose 0.7%, above the 0.4% forecast and the previous 0.3% gain, while disposable income increased 0.8%. Real disposable income recorded its largest rise since January, and the saving rate reached a three-month high. The BEA attributed part of the income increase to one-time Medicare Improvement Fund premium rebates, alongside continuing wage and salary gains. Fifth Third Commercial Bank's Bill Adams judged the broader spending trend solid despite October's pause; RSM's Joe Brusuelas emphasized the combination of strong aggregate demand and accelerating inflation as a reason for a policy response.

The inflation details sustained that disagreement with the softer monthly consumption result. Core PCE prices increased 0.3% in October, matching both the prior pace and consensus, but their annual rise accelerated to 3.3% from 3.1%, exceeding the 3.2% forecast and reaching the fastest pace since 2023. Headline PCE rose 0.3% monthly after 0.5% and 3.8% annually after 3.7%, both in line with expectations. Services prices excluding energy and housing increased 0.3%. The monthly spending pause consequently arrived with continued price pressure across goods and services.

Other releases showed continuing strength in hiring and investment intentions. Initial unemployment claims fell to 189,000 from 202,000, against a 200,000 consensus. Continuing claims declined to 1.697 million from 1.792 million, below the 1.721 million forecast. Orders for nondefense capital goods excluding aircraft rose 1.2% in October, above the expected 0.7% and the prior 0.5%. Total durable-goods orders increased only 0.2%, below the 0.6% forecast and September's 1.8%, while orders excluding transportation rose 0.5%, matching expectations and the previous month. The investment signal was stronger beneath the headline orders figure.

The Beige Book added breadth to the picture of persistent costs. Eight of the 12 Fed districts reported growth and four no change, with activity generally expanding slightly to moderately. Employment increased slightly. Wages and benefits rose moderately, an acceleration from the previous report's modest pace, concentrated in hard-to-fill positions and influenced by cost-of-living adjustments and benefit expenses. Contacts cited energy, transportation, healthcare, insurance, tariffs, raw materials and freight as sources of pressure. Competitive conditions and households' sensitivity to prices limited some firms' ability to pass those costs on. The survey, compiled by the Atlanta Fed, covered information collected through November 16.

Housing showed a similarly uneven response to high borrowing costs. October new-home sales increased 14.2% after a 9.7% decline, while final building permits fell 7.2% after a 0.4% drop. MBA mortgage applications rose 6.1%, reversing a 2.3% decrease; its purchase index increased to 151.6 from 137.6, while refinancing barely improved. The MBA's 30-year mortgage rate edged up to 7.38% from 7.35%.

A separate Bloomberg examination of homebuilders showed how incentives were supporting sales at the expense of profitability. The S&P Composite 1500 Homebuilding Index was down 0.9% for the year through Tuesday and 16% below its February peak, heading for a third annual loss. Expected 2027 gross margins at Meritage, Lennar and NVR were at multiyear lows. Evercore ISI's Stephen Kim cited labor shortages and longer construction cycles as additional costs, while Bloomberg Intelligence's Drew Reading said a sustained decline in rates driven by cooling inflation would offer a stronger demand catalyst than one accompanying economic deterioration.

Treasury's seven-year auction cleared at 4.71%, compared with 4.89% at the previous sale. Bid-to-cover eased to 2.43 from 2.46. The lower auction yield brought the week's supply into a substantially stronger government-bond market, while the small decline in coverage left demand short of an unqualified improvement on the preceding result.

## AI Borrowers Face a Sharper Credit Divide

The technology selloff produced another substantial increase in the price of default protection for CoreWeave. Five-year CDS rose as much as 2.09 percentage points, a record daily increase, to 15.34 percentage points annually, according to ICE Data Services. Bloomberg reported that the swaps implied a probability above 70% of default within five years. That market-implied assessment rose alongside record protection costs for Nvidia, Alphabet, Oracle and SpaceX as investors questioned the returns on the industry's borrowing-funded expansion.

CoreWeave's cash bonds reflected the same pressure. Its 9% notes due in 2031 traded at record lows to yield about 18%, according to TRACE. Yet the company's bankers at Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group were preparing a $4.5 billion loan sale for as soon as the following week, with initial yield discussions around 7%-7.5%. Potential investors had registered indications of interest in line with the proposed transaction's size, people familiar with the preparations said. Details and timing remained subject to change.

The proposed loan has a different repayment structure from CoreWeave's unsecured corporate debt. Proceeds would sit in escrow and be drawn to fund GPUs for a data center in Dalton, Georgia, with the equipment serving Meta Platforms. The debt is expected to amortize over its life and carry investment-grade ratings because of the Meta contract, even though CoreWeave itself is rated below investment grade. Its delayed-draw term loans were trading around par. The pricing discussions showed how a named customer, collateral and staged funding could produce a substantially different financing cost from that on the company's unsecured bonds.

The scale of construction remains substantial. Core Scientific is developing facilities across five states, fully leased to CoreWeave under a 12-year contract that could generate about $10 billion in revenue. CoreWeave reported $14.5 billion of capital expenditure in Q3, bringing spending for the first nine months to $30.65 billion. The new loan would finance another part of that buildout while corporate bondholders demanded much higher compensation for exposure to the overall business.

Nvidia acquired a distinct ratings catalyst. S&P placed its AA grade on CreditWatch with negative implications for a 90-day review, citing vulnerabilities in management and governance following Jensen Huang's departure and reinstatement. S&P expected any downgrade to be limited to one notch unless the company's future business prospects had been harmed. The review also encompasses questions about potential export-control violations and the effectiveness of the board's structure and composition.

Huang's Monday return had initially relieved concern about leadership at the center of the AI ecosystem. S&P's action shifted attention to the governance consequences of that reversal. Nvidia has about $32.5 billion of bonds in the U.S. high-grade corporate index, and its importance extends to financing and equipment supplied to other AI companies. Five-year CDS increased as much as 6 basis points to an intraday record of 147.27 basis points annually. Moody's kept its outlook unchanged Wednesday, citing continuing governance and regulatory uncertainty after previously moving the outlook on its Aa1 rating to stable from positive.

The selloff was beginning to produce disagreement about valuation. In a November 20 interview published Wednesday, DoubleLine's Robert Cohen said the firm had begun buying AI-related debt after yields and spreads improved. He pointed to AA-rated Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft bonds trading at spreads more typical of BBB debt, and also saw value in investment-grade SpaceX securities trading at yields associated with high yield. He was examining Oracle, whose spreads exceeded those of similarly rated companies.

Cohen drew a firmer boundary around unsecured debt from speculative-grade neoclouds. He questioned whether CoreWeave had a sustainable capital structure and a fully funded business plan, comparing the financing risks to those of the earlier shale expansion. His distinction was between borrowers and claims within the same investment cycle. Allspring's Mark Clegg likewise saw more value in AI bonds after the decline but said price discovery was continuing. Meanwhile, falling Treasury yields supported bond-fund returns: LQD gained 0.48% including distributions, compared with 0.12% for HYG.

Fresh JPMorgan research quantified how much financing the industry could still require. Strategists led by Tarek Hamid and Nathaniel Rosenbaum forecast AI-related capital spending nearly doubling to $1.4 trillion in 2027 before leveling off in 2028. They expected $450 billion of public investment-grade borrowing next year, up from $368 billion for AI-focused companies this year, plus $65 billion of leveraged finance and $25 billion-$35 billion of securitized products.

Their longer-range estimate envisaged 151 gigawatts of data-center capacity costing $7 trillion over 2027-2031. Because projects take years to construct and funding is raised upfront, much of the 2027 buildout was already paid for; borrowing next year would increasingly finance 2028 activity. With debt markets approaching capacity limits at the projected scale, JPMorgan estimated that $2.9 trillion of equity, largely from hyperscalers' organic cash flow, would be required over five years. It also expected the financing mix to shift toward hardware, with GPU funding needs potentially exceeding those for power shells by four times in 2031.

Those projections differ materially across firms. Goldman Sachs expects hyperscaler AI capital expenditure to rise 50% to $1.2 trillion next year, while Entext forecasts growth slowing to about 25%. JPMorgan identified a possible quarter in late 2027 or early 2028 when the following quarter's spending outlook would be approximately flat. That would make debt supply more predictable while leaving investors to assess a much slower growth rate after years of rapid expansion.

In Asia, tighter U.S. restrictions on Chinese access to advanced chips were already changing lending decisions. Bankers were pausing billions of dollars of loans to ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent, according to people familiar with the matter. Citigroup, Standard Chartered, DBS and other lenders were reviewing data-center clients and seeking more detail about chip users and compliance with the Commerce Department's rules. Neoclouds renting computing power and private investors backing Asian operators were among those receiving questions.

The pressure was also reaching asset-sale negotiations. A BlackRock- and IFM-backed consortium was considering reducing the equity portion of its offer for Stack Infrastructure's Asia-Pacific data centers and making some later payments contingent on project delivery. Talks had involved an enterprise value of $20 billion-$25 billion for assets in Japan, Australia and Malaysia; debt and planned capital expenditure would leave the equity value substantially below that amount. Local opposition, power and water constraints, approvals and uncertainty over Chinese remote demand complicated the valuation of development pipelines.

BDA Partners' Paul DiGiacomo said underlying demand had not cracked, while arguing that some platforms had been valued like technology companies despite heavy debt and uncertain capacity delivery. Liquid Compute's Ronit Jain said some Asian operators were trying to sell excess computing capacity to U.S. customers after the tighter chip rules disrupted plans to serve Chinese users. These are different manifestations of the same commercial adjustment: lenders are examining permitted users more closely while buyers reconsider how much to pay for capacity still to be delivered.

Alibaba was also holding preliminary discussions with banks about a possible offshore yuan or dollar bond sale next year and working toward an issuance quota from China's National Development and Reform Commission. Pictet Asset Management's Cary Yeung expected demand for Chinese hyperscaler bonds to remain supported by attractive all-in yields and relatively limited supply, while identifying access to advanced chips as an important concern. The talks remained preliminary, with market volatility among the factors governing any eventual offering.

## Financing Plans Encounter Uneven Market Access

The disruption in credit reached an issuer backed by one of Canada's largest pension managers. CDP Infrastructures, the issuing entity for La Caisse's infrastructure financing platform, paused an inaugural offering of as much as C$1 billion. People familiar with the sale said worsening market conditions would have required wider spreads and possibly a smaller issue.

Marketing for the prospective five-year bonds had begun around 70 basis points over government debt the previous week. By early this week, the spread had increased at least 5 basis points. The issuer, provisionally rated AA by Morningstar DBRS, was likely to revisit the transaction later. Alphabet's C$6 billion sale the previous week had also left investors digesting a large addition to Canadian corporate supply. In Europe, Deutsche Pfandbriefbank postponed a sterling offering, the region's first pulled high-grade deal of 2026.

Rakuten faced a more issuer-specific funding setback. It withdrew a planned approximately JPY150 billion subordinated bond sale on Tuesday, citing various circumstances and leaving future issuance timing undecided. The company declined to say whether the decision was influenced by the data breach at Rakuten Securities, which confirmed that about 4.41 million customer records had leaked. At 6:30 a.m. Wednesday in Tokyo, five-year CDS were about 29 basis points wider at roughly 262 basis points, the largest increase since April 2025. The canceled issue added to funding concerns while Rakuten's mobile business continued to record losses.

Large acquisition financings were still being proposed. Banks offered CVC as much as EUR11 billion of debt for a possible takeover of Verisure, including leveraged loans aimed at banks and institutional investors and high-yield bonds. Private-credit firms were seeking a role in junior debt. CVC was studying an offer, with Hellman & Friedman, which still owns about 44%, likely to retain an investment if a deal proceeded. Verisure's shares rose on the news after losing around a fifth since its Stockholm listing. Discussions remained ongoing, with no certainty of an offer.

Vietnam's HDBank outlined a different route to international funding. Chairman Kim Byoungho said it planned up to $500 million of global bonds, likely with a three-year maturity, and was discussing a $600 million syndicated loan. It aimed to complete both by year-end, or otherwise in Q1 2027. The proposed bonds would make it the first Vietnamese bank to list debt in the UK. Kim described the bank's $721 million July syndicated loan as substantially oversubscribed.

The fundraising comes as Vietnamese credit growth outpaces deposits. HDBank's lending target is about 35% this year, partly reflecting its role in restructuring a smaller lender, against a system-wide target near 15%. The central bank injected almost VND50 trillion through a $2 billion six-month foreign-exchange swap this month and also bought dollars outright from lenders. Fitch expects major Vietnamese banks to raise more than $6.9 billion by the end of next year, while warning that the capital drive is unlikely to improve most banks' still-thin capitalization materially. Kim emphasized the need to protect asset quality and capital adequacy as lending expands.

In U.S. municipals, Firecrest Aerospace secured an irrevocable JPMorgan letter of credit for a planned $10 million variable-rate bond sale through Stevens Point, Wisconsin. The bonds mature in 2046 and would fund a drone-engine manufacturing facility, with pricing expected December 1. Fitch assigned AA/F1+ based on JPMorgan's support. The letter can meet principal and interest payments but expires December 1, 2027 unless extended or replaced; parent Czechoslovak Group guarantees Firecrest's obligations to the bank. The long bond maturity and shorter bank-support term are central features of the financing.

## Inflation Complicates the Global Rate Outlook

Australia's inflation release challenged the recent shift toward earlier rate cuts. The annual trimmed-mean measure accelerated to 3.8% in October, above the 3.6% forecast, and core prices rose 0.5% monthly. Headline inflation reached 4.9%, exceeding the expected 4.7%. Housing costs increased 6.4% annually, electricity 25.2% and new dwellings 5.1%, while automotive fuel rose 6.3% during the month.

The Australian dollar gained 0.2% after the release, and the policy-sensitive three-year bond yield rose 4 basis points to 4.52%. Meeting-linked pricing put the probability of a May cut at 30%, down from 57% before the figures. The RBA had raised its cash rate to 4.85% earlier in November in a split decision, and its forecasts show underlying inflation falling below the top of its 2%-3% target only in late 2027.

The growth constraint remained important. October employment had fallen by 43,500 and unemployment reached a five-year high, while housing and business conditions weakened. Most economists and traders still regarded the hiking cycle as complete. Nomura's Andrew Ticehurst expected the RBA to remain hawkish for months even if inflation was near a peak. Commonwealth Bank's Hamid Yahyaei described the immediate bond selloff as relatively contained, suggesting investors retained conviction that cuts would arrive in 2027. The inflation surprise delayed expected relief without erasing the labor-market argument for it.

Japan released two distinct measures pointing to persistent prices. Corporate service costs increased 4.2% annually in October from a revised 3.8%, the fastest rise since 1990. Ocean freight charges surged 120.4%, a record in data beginning in 1986, as the Iran war disrupted transport. Separately, the BOJ's consumer-price measure excluding fresh food and special factors accelerated to 3.5% from 3.2%, its fastest pace since September 2023. That measure strips out temporary assistance including gasoline and utility subsidies, explaining its stronger reading than the government's 2.2% CPI measure excluding fresh food.

The inflation evidence arrived alongside a clearer borrowing-cost burden. Almost 59% of companies in a Teikoku Databank survey said the negative effects of higher rates outweighed the positive, up 14 percentage points from December. About 48% had been approached by their main banks about higher loan rates; among those firms, 29% had already experienced an increase. Average rates on new loans reached 2.12% in September, the highest since 1996. Those responses describe firms' experience of tightening as the BOJ weighs another move from its 1.25% policy rate.

Demand at Japan's 40-year auction was weaker. Bid-to-cover fell to 2.63 from 3.10 at the previous sale and below the 12-month average of 2.75. The auction yield was 4.09%, compared with 4.125% previously. BNP Paribas Asset Management's Ryutaro Kimura linked the result to global risk aversion and unwinding curve-flattening positions, with investors preferring shorter maturities to super-long debt. Uncertainty over financing defense expenditure and a consumption-tax cut in the fiscal 2027 budget remained relevant to prospective issuance.

Japan's largest pension fund supplied a potential longer-term demand development, though its interpretation remained disputed. GPIF discussed its basic portfolio at a November 13 board meeting. JPMorgan strategist Junya Tanase said the agenda could indicate that a review had advanced to consideration of allocation changes and that a revision might occur as early as the first half of next year. He explicitly described that interpretation as speculative. GPIF said the investment environment had not diverged significantly from its assumptions and that it would consider changes if necessary. Its target remains 25% in each of domestic bonds, foreign bonds, domestic equities and foreign equities.

In Britain, Governor Andrew Bailey and Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli added consequential voices to the case for further tightening. Testifying to Parliament, Bailey said more increases were more likely than not if energy prices failed to fall. He described the economy as more resilient than expected and the labor market as flattening out rather than continuing to soften. Lombardelli said the anticipated decline in wages and services inflation might have stalled and saw accumulating evidence of second-round effects.

Their positions matter to the December coalition. Markets assigned an almost 80% probability to an increase, while most economists expected a hold until February. Support from Bailey and Lombardelli would likely create a majority on the nine-member MPC alongside members already seeking another rise. Catherine Mann maintained her preference for early, forceful action after favoring a half-point increase in November, arguing that economic resilience suggested insufficient restraint.

There was still disagreement about how widely the energy shock was spreading. Bailey said businesses reported difficulty passing costs through, and the December decision would depend on that transmission and another round of inflation and labor data. Swati Dhingra said she had not seen second-round effects and put the affected share of the consumption basket near 20%, compared with 70% at a similar stage in 2022. She described her support for November's increase as additional insurance. The BOE expects inflation to approach 5% by next summer, with the household energy-price cap raising bills 26% in January and potentially further in April.

ECB Governing Council member Martin Kocher separately argued for acting before inflation became more entrenched. The Austrian central-bank chief viewed the outlook as somewhat worse than the September projections and expected December forecasts for 2027 inflation to require upward revision because of higher forward energy prices. Markets fully priced another increase beyond December, an outlook he considered reasonable on current information.

Kocher distinguished the continuing supply shock from strong demand-driven inflation, which he was not yet observing. Anecdotal second-round effects could become clearer in the first half of 2027 as wage negotiations concluded. He also cautioned against treating economic resilience as permanent. In a separate operational discussion Wednesday, ECB officials remained divided over increasing banks' minimum reserve requirement to 2% from 1%; people familiar with the seminar said a decision could wait until 2027. That timing moved the reserve debate away from an imminent change in bank liquidity requirements.

## Pension Inflows and Fiscal Constraints Divide Emerging Debt

India's pension industry offered a new source of government-bond demand as recovering stocks pushed equity allocations toward regulatory limits. UTI Pension Fund is directing half of incremental investments into sovereign debt, compared with none last year. SBI Pension Funds expects equities to take only about a quarter of new investments, down from roughly 60% in the three months through June. Together the two managers account for 58% of India's $193 billion retirement market.

The reallocation reverses an earlier preference for equities after the regulator increased their permitted portfolio weight to 25% from 15% in March 2025. Government bonds received only 23% of new pension investment through October this year, compared with 55% in the fiscal year ended March 2025. The Nifty's approximately 14% recovery from its October low has now reduced the room for additional stock purchases. Pension inflows could support sovereign borrowing after heavy federal and state supply helped push the 10-year government yield more than 60 basis points higher this year.

South Africa's central bank examined a different competition for long-term savings. In its financial stability review Wednesday, it warned that AI companies' borrowing could increase sovereign funding costs as governments compete for the same capital. The domestic collective investment schemes it analyzed held almost 13% of assets in AI-related companies by Q3, with more than two-thirds of that exposure concentrated in Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet. Naspers and Prosus provided an additional indirect link through about 8% of Johannesburg's equity-market value.

The review described possible channels from a global repricing to South Africa through portfolio outflows, currency depreciation and higher government yields. Refinancing needs make the timing important: maturing sovereign debt will approach or exceed ZAR400 billion annually from the end of the decade through 2032. The central bank nevertheless judged the financial system resilient. Preliminary stress tests indicated banks would remain above regulatory capital requirements in a severe downturn, although buffers would be reduced; full results are due in early 2027.

The IMF's new assessment focused on the fiscal adjustment required to reduce those borrowing pressures. It endorsed spending prudence and debt stabilization but urged explicit debt objectives, expenditure ceilings, primary-balance targets and correction mechanisms to strengthen the government's principles-based fiscal anchor. Reaching debt near 70% of GDP by 2033 would require primary-balance consolidation of 0.5% of GDP annually over the next three years, the Fund estimated. It also recommended reallocating 1% of GDP from current expenditure toward more efficient public investment over the medium term.

The IMF projected a primary surplus of 1.4% of GDP this year and 1.8% over the medium term, enough to stabilize debt around 75% of GDP. Treasury's projections were stronger, at 1.7% this year and 2.9% in 2029-2030. Wage negotiations, state-enterprise liabilities, municipal debt and weaker revenue remained risks. The IMF also supported moderately restrictive monetary policy to return inflation to the central bank's 3% target, with further tightening possible if risks materialized.

Thailand's budget arithmetic exposed a nearer political constraint. A Budget Bureau projection put room for development and investment outside day-to-day spending at about THB674 billion next fiscal year, potentially a record low, even assuming VAT rises to 8.5% from 7%. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has ruled out that increase, while Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas has pledged not to raise the 70%-of-GDP debt ceiling. Debt already stood at 68.6% at September-end.

Current expenditure is projected to absorb about 82% of the budget in fiscal 2028, up from 76% in 2026, leaving investment vulnerable to any effort to reconcile those commitments. Thailand's debt structure provides funding stability: more than 99% is denominated in baht and average maturity exceeds nine years. Moody's identified sustained deterioration in growth and public finances relative to similarly rated countries as the more important credit risk; S&P expects growth of only about 2.3%-2.4% annually through 2029. All three major agencies currently assign stable outlooks.

The government's revenue measures include widening the tax base, reviewing incentives and taxing low-value online imports. Implementation is difficult in an economy where central-bank research puts 78% of businesses and 65% of workers in the informal sector, and only about 4 million of a 40 million workforce pay personal income tax. A proposed outbound-travel tax was dropped after criticism, foregoing an estimated THB12 billion annually. The medium-term plan due next week must reconcile limited revenue options with the approaching debt ceiling.

## Forward Market Significance

The U.S. Thanksgiving closure on Thursday and shortened Friday bond session reduce the time available for markets to absorb Wednesday's concentrated economic news. December tightening remains central to expectations, but the next assessment must reconcile 3.3% core PCE inflation and strong revised Q3 growth with flat October real consumption and the effect of volatile financial conditions. The initial equity rebound leaves open whether the adjustment in technology finance continues to tighten access to capital.

CoreWeave's prospective $4.5 billion loan sale as soon as next week provides a direct financing test. Final pricing, size and distribution will show how investors value its Meta-linked collateral and repayment structure while unsecured yields remain elevated. Nvidia's 90-day S&P review turns on governance and regulatory risks, with a larger-than-one-notch downgrade dependent on damage to future business prospects. In Asia, the outstanding questions are how lenders complete their chip-compliance reviews and how Stack's proposed buyers allocate construction and delivery risks in any revised offer.

Washington's newly outlined tariffs add a separate conditional risk to demand and prices. The announced framework would put imports from China at 20%, with a senior U.S. official describing a possible increase to 40% if trade talks fail. The EU, Japan, South Korea and Switzerland would face 15%; India's proposed 17% depends on finalizing a trade pact. China's foreign ministry urged preservation of the trade truce. Negotiations and implementation will determine the extent of the next trade shock.

Britain's December 17 decision and Japan's December 18 meeting now follow fresh evidence about inflation persistence and the burden of higher borrowing costs. For the BOE, forthcoming labor and price releases will inform the disagreement about energy pass-through. For the BOJ, accelerating subsidy-adjusted inflation sits alongside firms' reports of more expensive credit. Australia's policy outlook similarly depends on whether weakening employment is followed by moderation in prices after October's upside surprise. Thailand's medium-term fiscal plan next week supplies a nearer sovereign decision, with the VAT assumption and the commitment to retain the debt ceiling still to be reconciled.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries rally into the long end as technology losses spur demand for safety
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasury demand extended to the long end during another technology selloff. The 10-year yield fell 7.56 basis points to 4.8541% and the 30-year declined 7.24 basis points to 5.2479%. A 7.93-basis-point fall in the 10-year real yield drove the nominal rally; breakeven inflation edged 0.37 basis point higher as oil recovered. The Nasdaq 100 pared an intraday loss of as much as 4.7% to close 0.64% lower, leaving government bonds supported even after stocks recovered much of their decline.

The economic releases combined flat October real consumer spending with core PCE inflation accelerating to 3.3% annually and Q3 GDP growth revised to 4.3%. Softer monthly consumption supported the demand case for bonds, while persistent price pressure sustained expectations of December tightening.

Credit stress became more differentiated. S&P put Nvidia's AA rating under a 90-day review for possible downgrade over governance and regulatory risks. CoreWeave's default-protection costs reached a record and its unsecured bonds yielded about 18%, while bankers prepared a prospective $4.5 billion loan with initial yield discussions around 7%-7.5%. Its Meta-linked collateral, staged funding and expected amortization distinguished that proposed financing from unsecured corporate exposure. Final loan terms and distribution, potentially as soon as next week, will test access to funding as technology valuations adjust.
